title: Giovanni Mazzinghi's cipher letter of 16 January 1478, bare; the same cipher is glossed in MAP 72/170 a week later
correspondents: Giovanni Mazzinghi -> (the Medici; addressee not named on the page)
place: not stated (Rome likely: the sibling letter reports papal news)
shelfmark: Archivio di Stato di Firenze, Mediceo avanti il Principato, filza LXXXIX, doc. 142 (old c. 149)
folio_note: One leaf, recto full of cipher (about 45 lines, some clear words between runs); verso blank but endorsed "1478 ... adi 16 di gennaio ... Gio. Mazinghi" and "Cifra". Inventory vol. 3: "Giovanni Mazzinghi. (cifrato). s. l., 1478 gen. 16, n. 142".
status: No decipherment on, over or beside the cipher (checked at 1600 px). The sign set (x, ‡, H, =, 5-like signs) is the one of MAP LXXII doc. 170 (23 Jan 1478), which carries a full interlinear decipherment.
why: A pre-1497 Florentine cipher letter of the Medici circle in the months around the Pazzi conspiracy, unread on the page, with a glossed sibling in the same system: a short route to a reading.
verify: Transcribe MAP 72/170, build the key from its interlinear pairs, apply it to 89/142; check the date style and Mazzinghi's post (Rome?) in the letter itself.

vetting_note: Leaf c. 13r seen in Chrome on the BNCF teca viewer (idr BNCF0003827870, thumbnail grid): a strip with four lines of symbol cipher (digits, letters, Greek-like signs, about 75 per line, roughly 300 in all), no gloss. But the strip just before it, c. 12r (same narrow format, stamped 3423195), is a clear Italian note: "El conte Girolamo ha sollecitato l'andata di m. Ascanio a Roma, qual si stima sia opera dello S.re ... el Palavisino ... m. Johanfrancesco ... Strasoldano è sospecto assai parendo loro che lui sia ghibellino", about 300 letters. Two quick checks suggest it may be the clear of c. 13r: the cipher's "11" pair falls where the "ll" of "sollecitato" (line 1) and "ghibellino" (end) would be, and a near-repeat ("s q s 3 n m π b t" / "s y s 3 n π b t") fits the two "Palavisino" at matching positions. A full alignment was not done. Edition check: archive.org full-text search of Lorenzo de' Medici, Lettere V, VI and VII (bwb_KU-999-230_5, -229_6, -231) finds GC 137 cited only for cc. 4, 6-9, 20-21, 22-23/26/35, 32-33/47, 38-39, 45-46, 48-51, never c. 13. The Censimento (1964, Google Books seEYGFQqM1kC) has "137, c. 13" on p. 48 together with 1481, giu/lug/ago, Michelozzi, Ridolfi, Milano: a Lorenzo letter of summer 1481, entry text not readable. Next: align c. 13r with c. 12r. If it fits, the verdict is read (contemporary clear); if not, the lead is open.
